newsitem.title: USA: U.S. envoy Ross to go to Mideast this week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy Ross to go to Mideast this week.

text.p: U.S. envoy Dennis Ross will go to the Middle East this week for talks with Israeli and Palestinian leaders on reviving the stalled peace process, Secretary of State Madeleine Albright announced Monday.

Albright said Ross would consult with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat "on how to stem violence and what steps they are prepared to take to stop the deterioration and lay the basis for making the peace process work again."

On the basis of Ross's talks, U.S. President Bill Clinton would be able to decide "what the United States can and will do to re-establish the credibility of the process", Albright told reporters before a meeting with Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec.

Israeli-Palestinian talks have been deadlocked since January, in part due to a dispute over a new Israeli housing project in mainly Arab East Jerusalem, which has led to almost daily Palestinian demonstrations.
"There has been a serious deterioration in the level of trust and confidence and in the ability of the parties to pursue peace," Albright said.
